claims.text: The initial material is equal-atomic, single-phase BCC NbMoTaW.
Adding a small amount of titanium to NbMoTaW will improve its room-temperature ductility.
Adding a small amount of zirconium to NbMoTaW will improve its room-temperature ductility.
Titanium- or zirconium-alloyed NbMoTaW will maintain the high-temperature mechanical properties of untreated NbMoTaW.
Titanium- or zirconium-alloyed NbMoTaW will maintain or enhance irradiation tolerance relative to untreated NbMoTaW under helium implantation.
The alloyed material will preserve BCC structural stability.
Titanium or zirconium addition will enhance atomic diffusion in NbMoTaW.
Titanium or zirconium addition will enhance atomic redistribution in NbMoTaW.
Titanium or zirconium addition may produce solid-solution strengthening in NbMoTaW.
The proposed performance balance is applicable from room temperature through 1600 °C.
The proposed irradiation response is applicable to helium implantation energies up to several hundred keV.

The hypothesis can be tested by comparing helium-implanted alloyed and unalloyed NbMoTaW using tensile tests at room temperature and 1600 °C and measurements of ductility, yield strength, and microstructure.
No improvement in room-temperature ductility or a significant loss of high-temperature mechanical properties would falsify the hypothesis.
